newsitem.title: GERMANY: More rye offered into German grain intervention.
newsitem.headline: More rye offered into German grain intervention.

text.p: Nearly 40,000 tonnes of rye were offered into German grain intervention stores last week, weekly figures from state intervention board BLE showed.
Barley and wheat were also increasingly finding their way into the stores.
But totals in the November-May 1996/97 season still lag those in the same 95/96 period.
Volumes on Feb 14 totalled 585,661 tonnes compared with 1,403,804 tonnes a year earlier.
The figure described volumes accepted, but not yet delivered to stores, by the close last Friday.
Feed rye and and barley were headed for intervention as cheap feed wheat continued to dominate the feed grain market and pressurised the prices of other cereals, including bread wheat, traders said.
Free market bread wheat and rye prices held up above the Feb intervention buying-in price of 241.52 marks a tonne.
